title: Probe timing & KEDA cooldown interaction caused scale-down cascade and large cold-start spike
creator: Priya Natarajan
body: Summary: On 2026-03-05 at ~03:42 UTC we observed a production incident affecting the inference request surface for our chat-routing service. Symptoms included a sudden spike in 5xx errors and 99th percentile latency for ~22 minutes for customers routed to region eu-west-1. The root cause was an interaction between misconfigured Kubernetes probes, an init-container that delayed readiness export of request metrics, and KEDA's scaler cooldown/stabilization settings which led to a rapid cascade of scale-downs to zero followed by slow scale-up (cold starts). This ticket documents the timeline, technical cause, immediate mitigations, and long-term action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 03:42 UTC — Grafana alert fired: chat-routing:request_5xx_rate > 1% for 5m
03:43 — Pager duty: SRE oncall paged (Liam). Investigation started; initial dashboards showed pods decreasing from 8 -> 0 in 4 minutes.
03:46 — Engineering confirmed KEDA ScaledObject for chat-routing had scaledDown to 0 replicas; HPA minReplicas was 0. Pods were terminating due to liveness probe failures tied to startup sequence.

03:50 — Rollback/mitigation: temporarily disabled KEDA scaledown by patching ScaledObject minReplicaCount=1 and bumped HPA minReplicas=1 to restore baseline capacity; synthetic traffic rps=5/s sent to trigger warmup.
04:05 — Traffic normalized; 5xx rate returned to baseline. Incident declared mitigated at 04:12 UTC. Post-incident investigation began and root cause analysis completed by 2026-03-09.
root_cause: A combination of three factors: (1) readiness probe timing was too aggressive (initialDelaySeconds=5, periodSeconds=10) leading k8s to consider pods unready during JVM/model load; (2) the init container that sets up model weights blocks the Prometheus exporter endpoint until it finishes, so the KEDA scaler's metric (requests_per_second provided by the exporter) reported near-zero during startup; and (3) KEDA's cooldown/stabilization window (default 30s) plus ScaledObject scale-to-zero policy allowed quick scale-downs to 0 instead of maintaining a small warm pool. The net effect: controller saw low metrics, scaled to zero, requests routed produced cold-starts that exposed the startup delay and further contributed to errors during the warmup window.
immediate_mitigation: Patched ScaledObject in eu-west-1: set minReplicaCount=1 to prevent scale-to-zero for high-traffic endpoints (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-configs/pull/712)
Bumped HPA minReplicas=1 for chat-routing (hotfix commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/commit/9f3a2d7)
Added temporary synthetic keepalive traffic to chat-routing for 15 minutes to accelerate pod warmup
Increased liveness/readiness initialDelaySeconds to 60s for model-server pods as a short-term safety net
long_term_action_items: ENG-52300: Move KEDA metrics to use queue_length (active requests in queue) instead of exporter RPS which is flaky during startup — owner: Mei Park — due: 2026-04-02

ENG-52301: Implement a warm-pool controller (small steady-state pool) for critical low-latency services to avoid scale-to-zero; design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Warm+Pool+Design — owner: Liam Chen — due: 2026-04-30

ENG-52302: Harden startup sequence: make Prometheus exporter available before init containers block metrics or decouple KEDA metric source from exporter — owner: SRE team (oncall rotation) — due: 2026-03-26
ENG-52303: Add KEDA stabilizationWindow and cooldown tuning per ScaledObject with conservative defaults and traffic-aware overrides — owner: Priya Natarajan — due: 2026-03-19
ENG-52304: Add automated integration test that simulates init-container delay and verifies scaler doesn't scale-to-zero for endpoints with traffic above threshold — owner: QA — due: 2026-04-09

ENG-52305: Update runbooks/alerting: differentiate scale-to-zero incidents vs runtime errors in alert messages; add playbook steps (scale minReplica, inject synthetic traffic) — owner: SRE — due: 2026-03-18
postmortem_notes: Decision trade-offs: We chose to set minReplicaCount=1 quickly to stop customer impact; this increases baseline cost but is acceptable for critical routes until a warm-pool solution ships.

We debated whether to change the metric KEDA consumes vs making exporter available earlier. Short-term we will prefer metric re-targeting (queue_length) to avoid tight coupling with exporter lifecycle.

Engineering review requested: runtime team to audit other services using the same exporter pattern; early scan found 8 other scaledObjects referencing exporter RPS metric — follow-up assigned (ENG-52306).
comments: 2026-03-05 04:00 UTC — Liam Chen: Initial mitigation applied; scaling floor set to 1. Monitoring shows error rate falling. Following up with deeper RCA.
2026-03-06 09:12 UTC — Priya Natarajan: Confirmed init-container blocks prom exporter. Created ENG-52302 to decouple exporter startup. Temporary probe increases pushed to canary.
2026-03-07 14:45 UTC — Mei Park: Ran replay test simulating exporter delay; KEDA scale-to-zero happens within 35s when RPS drops to 0. Raised proposal to switch to queue_length metric (ENG-52300).
2026-03-08 11:10 UTC — SRE: Added playbook steps to incident runbook; added alert annotation to distinguish scale-induced 5xx vs upstream failure.
2026-03-09 16:20 UTC — Priya Natarajan: Postmortem drafted; steering review scheduled. Action items and owners assigned. Closing incident after verification of mitigations on 2026-03-10.
verification_and_closure: 2026-03-10 — Verified that scaledObjects with new minReplica policy did not regress over 72h in eu-west-1 canary cluster.
2026-03-11 — Smoke tests for synthetic warmup passed; no increase in baseline error rate; cost impact <3% for the service.
Closure: Incident retired after 72h of stable metrics; long-term tickets created for follow-up work.
